pairs.subject: render-mount-pipeline
pairs.evidence: app/foundry/pipeline/PipelineCanvas.tsx:79 PipelineCanvas delegates card mounting to React component mappings over culled item placements rather than executing an incremental render-mount pipeline with a unit blueprint, reference counting, and recycling pools.

techniques.evidence: app/foundry/pipeline/Card.tsx:134 Each card mounts nested arranging host DOM elements rather than collapsing layout into a flat blueprint of render units where non-promoted arranging containers vanish.

app/foundry/pipeline/Card.tsx:80 Cards handle updating via component-level memoization comparing props rather than separating mount-clock content binders and attach-clock event binders with undo lifecycles.
app/foundry/pipeline/Card.tsx:64 In-flight and dragged items rely on a boolean flag to dim the home slot instead of holding per-unit reference counts across competing features.

app/foundry/pipeline/CellLayer.tsx:99 Visible cells are iterated and mounted across lane slices on layout updates rather than using two edge-sorted boundary indices and cursors to bound mounting work to boundary crossings.
app/foundry/pipeline/CellLayer.tsx:98 Host cell elements are allocated directly into an array on each render instead of being acquired from and returned to a recycling pool keyed by content type.
app/foundry/pipeline/PipelineCanvas.tsx:68 Layout computation is consumed synchronously on the main thread without supporting shared, continuable layout execution across different waiter classes.
